## 2

That’s definitely one of the more creative rabbit holes out there! But while I can appreciate a lively imagination, the science behind our spinning, spherical Earth is rock-solid—and honestly, even more wondrous than any conspiracy. From ships dipping hull-first over the horizon to the curved shadow our planet casts during a lunar eclipse, humans have actually known we live on a globe for thousands of years, well before modern space photography came along! 

## 3

Think of sunlight like a team of colors traveling together in waves. Red and orange light travel in long, lazy, slow waves, while blue light travels in short, energetic, choppy little waves! 

When sunlight hits Earth’s atmosphere, it runs into billions of tiny gas molecules. The long red and yellow waves pass right through them without much trouble, but those tiny, bouncy blue waves bump into the air particles and scatter in every single direction—kind of like a handful of superballs bouncing off the walls of a room. When you look up during the day, you’re seeing all that scattered blue light bouncing right into your eyes!

## 4

夜幕低垂，细密的雨丝斜斜地织入黑暗，在昏黄的路灯下泛着柔和的微光。雨滴轻快地敲打着窗玻璃，宛如大自然悄悄弹奏的一曲舒缓小夜曲。街道上行人寥寥，湿漉漉的柏油路面映出斑斓倒影，像是一幅被水汽晕染开的水彩画。屋里弥漫着淡淡的书香与热茶的暖意，听着窗外淅淅沥沥的声响，整个喧嚣的世界仿佛都在这场夜雨中渐渐沉静下来。
